To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified and characterized two gene fragments, derived from the murine and human NPHS genes, that direct podocyte specific expression in transgenic animals, without expression in extranrenal tissues.
two gene fragments that direct specific podocyte expression in transgenic mouse models were identified.
two novel podocyte-specific gene promoters were identified and used to drive transgene expression specifically in podocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of gene fragments that direct transgene expression exclusively in podocytes.
the identification of podocyte-specific promoters that can be used to drive expression of transgenes of interest to investigate the role of podocyte-specific genes in glomerular biology and disease.
the development of a novel gene therapy strategy for the treatment of glomerulopathies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2. 5-kb NPSH2 promoter fragment may prove useful for podocyte specific transgenic expression when extra renal expression of a transgenic is problematic.
both the p1.25 N-nlacF and the p2.5p-nlacF transgenes are podocyte-specific and do not express in any other tissue in adult mice.
both promoter fragments are podocyte-specific in adult mice and both are not active in embryonic mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the 1.25 kb NPHS1 and 2.5 kb NPHS2 fragments drive expression in podocytes in transgenic mice, but not in extrarenal tissue, suggesting that the cis-regulatory elements responsible for expression in brain and pancreata are located elsewhere in the promoter regions of the NPHS1 or NPHS2 gene.
we have identified two podocyte-specific promoters that direct transgene expression in transgenic mouse podocytes.
the 1.25 kb NPHS1 gene fragment is more efficient than the 2.25 kb NPSH2 gene fragment in driving transgene expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a truly podocyte specific promoter.
podocyte-specific promoters are available for transgenic manipulation of this cell type in the future.
the Nphs2 promoter is a more reliable promoter to use in transgenic mice to achieve podocyte-specific expression.
